LI4.name: He Gu
LI4.location: In the webbing between the thumb and index finger, at the highest point of the muscle when they are pressed together.
LI4.technique: Pinch the webbing between your opposite thumb and index finger. Press firmly toward the bone of the index finger. Press for 3 seconds, release for 1 second.
LI4.caution: Avoid during pregnancy — this point is traditionally used to promote labour.

GB20.name: Feng Chi
GB20.location: In the two hollows at the base of the skull, between the two vertical neck muscles, about two finger-widths out from the spine.
GB20.technique: Interlock your fingers behind your head and press your thumbs upward and inward into the hollows. Let your head tip back into the pressure. Press for 3 seconds, release for 1 second.

PC6.name: Nei Guan
PC6.location: On the inner forearm, two thumb-widths above the wrist crease, in the dip between the two central tendons.
PC6.technique: Press with the thumb of your opposite hand, straight down between the tendons. Press for 3 seconds, release for 1 second.

ST36.name: Zu San Li
ST36.location: On the outer front of the shin, four finger-widths below the kneecap and one finger-width out from the shin bone.
ST36.technique: Press with your thumb or knuckle into the muscle beside the bone. Press for 3 seconds, release for 1 second.

SP6.name: San Yin Jiao
SP6.location: On the inner lower leg, four finger-widths above the inner ankle bone, just behind the edge of the shin bone.
SP6.technique: Press with your thumb into the soft tissue behind the bone. Press for 3 seconds, release for 1 second.
SP6.caution: Avoid during pregnancy — this point is traditionally used to promote labour.
